title: The query engine and the exposure log: typed plans that can never list rows, a row floor, and a record of every relation explored
request: Complete the Home plan package by package; H6 lets Home compute aggregates from the person's table without ever showing a row or giving a model the values.
spec: Package H6 of Phase H: a versioned typed query plan, a validator (no row listing; no free-text or identifier grouping), a pandas executor on the checked clean table, the row floor, an exposure log of every relation explored; purpose home_query (column summaries only); DCLAB_MODEL_READS_AGGREGATES and DCLAB_ROW_FLOOR on the Admin page and in .env.example. Done when: the H1 analysis requests' expected tables are reproduced by plans on the H1 tables, no plan can list rows, and the Admin page states the new limit.
plan: Write the plan's shape: filters, group_by (a few columns), an optional period with a grain, measures from a fixed list, sort and a limit; a plan hash for the log.

Validate against the table's column kinds: refuse identifiers, personal columns and free text as groups or filters, unknown columns and keys, operations that do not fit the kind, a measure-free plan; any malformed plan is a PlanError, never a crash.

Execute on the cleaned table read through the file store and checked against its recorded SHA-256; hide groups under the floor, and groups with too few different people; withhold extremes for small groups.
Log every plan run on the draft (columns related, the table and its hash) for the later holdout choice.
Let a model write a plan from column summaries only, one retry with the validator's reasons; state the limits on the Admin page and in .env.example.

decisions.decision: The package is dclab_rnd/query, not dclab_rnd/analysis as the plan says.
decisions.why: dclab_rnd/analysis.py already exists; a package of that name would shadow it.

decisions.decision: A plan has no way to ask for rows: every output column is a group key or an aggregate.
decisions.why: A rule against listing rows is easier to keep when the shape cannot express a listing than when a validator must spot one.

decisions.decision: Personal columns (email, phone, names, addresses, account numbers) are identifiers whatever their uniqueness.
decisions.why: A customer's email repeats across orders, so a uniqueness test calls it a category; grouping by it lists one person's orders.

decisions.decision: The floor counts different people as well as rows, and min, max and high percentiles of small groups are withheld.
decisions.why: Twelve orders of one customer pass a row floor; the maximum of a small group is often one row's value.

decisions.decision: The floor can be raised and never set below a fixed minimum; the Admin text says it is not anonymisation.
decisions.why: Differencing two allowed answers can still reveal a small group; saying so is more honest than promising privacy.

change: New dclab_rnd/query (plan.py, validate.py, execute.py, propose.py) and prompts/home_query.md; the home_query purpose (models/settings.py); draft/pipeline.py records the cleaned table's SHA-256; settings.py checks DCLAB_ROW_FLOOR; the Admin page's answers item (agentic/pages/platform.py) and .env.example state the floor and DCLAB_MODEL_READS_AGGREGATES. tests/test_query_engine.py; test_model_data_limits covers home_query. AEV-024.

findings.defect: A personal column could be a group or a filter.
findings.scenario: Grouping orders by email listed each customer's orders under their address, because an email that repeats looked like a category.
findings.cause: Identifiers were found by uniqueness and an _id name only.
findings.fix: Personal names (email, phone, person names, account, address, ip) and value shapes (email, phone) mark a column an identifier; camelCase ids are read case-sensitively so 'paid' is not one.

findings.defect: A group of one person's rows passed the floor.
findings.scenario: A city with a single customer and twelve orders showed that customer's total spend.
findings.fix: A group must also hold at least the floor's number of different values of every identifier column.

findings.defect: A hidden group's size came back as an exact count.
findings.scenario: Filtering to one VIP with a high salary returned no rows but rows_matched said exactly one.
findings.fix: rows_matched is reported only when no group was hidden.

findings.defect: Extremes of small groups showed single rows' values.
findings.scenario: The maximum salary of a group just above the floor was one person's salary.
findings.cause: Every measure was shown once a group passed the floor.
findings.fix: min, max and high percentiles are withheld for groups under a multiple of the floor and counted in withheld_extremes.

findings.defect: Malformed plans crashed instead of being refused.
findings.scenario: A sort given as a list of strings, a period given as a string, or a text value on a numeric filter raised TypeError from inside pandas.
findings.cause: The validator checked known shapes and let others through.
findings.fix: Every check runs inside one wrapper that turns any exception into a PlanError; values are type-checked against the column's kind.

findings.defect: Time-zone-aware dates and odd values broke the executor or the JSON.
findings.scenario: A tz-aware order date compared with a plain date raised; a Decimal group key did not serialise.
findings.cause: Dates and values were used as pandas gave them.
findings.fix: Dates are made naive before comparison; every output value is turned into a JSON type.

findings.defect: A group or measure named period collided with the period column.
findings.scenario: A plan with a grain and a measure called period returned two columns of that name.
findings.fix: With a grain, a group or measure named period is refused.

findings.defect: The exposure log did not say which table was explored, and the Admin page did not name the floor.
findings.scenario: After a table was replaced, the log could not tell which relations were explored on which version; an owner could not see the active floor.
findings.cause: The entry held the plan only; the Admin text was generic.
findings.fix: Each entry carries the asset and the table's SHA-256; the Admin item states the floor, its minimum, whether a model reads aggregates, and the differencing caveat.

outcome: Home can now compute an aggregate answer on the person's cleaned table from a plan that cannot list rows; small groups and single people are hidden, every relation explored is logged with its table, and a model that writes a plan sees only column summaries.
lessons: Uniqueness is a poor test for an identifier: a person's email repeats across their orders; the name and the value's shape say more.
A floor on rows is not a floor on people.
risks: Differencing two allowed answers can still reveal a small group; the floor narrows this but is not anonymisation, and the Admin page says so.
